title: Gurjara-Pratihara Dynasty
capsule: The Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty was the dominant power in northern India from the late 8th through the 10th century, with two lineages: the Harichandra line ruling Mandore in Rajasthan and the more powerful Nagabhata line, which from c. 730 blocked Arab armies advancing east of the Indus and made Kannauj the imperial capital of a realm spanning the Gangetic plain to Gujarat and Rajputana. Under Mihira Bhoja (r. c. 836–85) and his son Mahendrapala I the empire rivaled the Guptas in extent and supported a flourishing Sanskrit literary culture; the dynasty held the title Maharajadhiraja of Aryavarta and is associated with the Maru-Gurjara architectural tradition. Rashtrakuta raids from the south and feudatory rebellions steadily eroded Pratihara power in the 10th century, and Mahmud of Ghazni's capture of Kannauj in 1018 ended any residual authority; the dynasty formally survived as a minor principality until around 1036.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Core territories around Kannauj, Rajputana, and the Gangetic plain are documented through copper-plate grants and Arab accounts (notably al-Masudi); outer campaign-era boundaries and the western Rajputana extent are reconstructed from inscriptions and narrative sources and remain approximate.
